goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — A crash or Redis failure between SETNX and EXPIRE leaves a permanent throttle key, silently preventing that embed from ever being fetched.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 25-30, the code uses SETNX followed by EXPIRE as separate operations. If the process crashes or Redis connection fails between these two calls, the key would be set without an expiration, creating a permanent throttle key. This is a real race condition/reliability issue. The standard fix would be to use SET with EX/NX options in a single atomic operation (SET key value EX 60 NX). This is a legitimate bug that could cause embed URLs to be permanently blocked from retrieval.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — One malformed feed item can raise and abort the whole retry-disabled poll, so later items remain unimported as long as that entry is present.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the poll_feed method iterates over rss.items with `rss.items.each do |i|`. The job has `sidekiq_options retry: false` set. If any item in the feed causes an exception (e.g., malformed content, nil values causing NoMethodError on .scrub, invalid URL format), the entire job will abort and no retry will occur. This means subsequent items in the feed won't be processed. The code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` which could raise if i.content is nil, and `TopicEmbed.import` could also raise on various conditions. This is a real robustness issue - one bad feed item prevents processing of all remaining items.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:7 — A failed or skipped retrieval has no terminal state, so every active embed reloads forever and continually enqueues more retrieval jobs.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code flow: embed/loading.html.erb reloads every 30 seconds. The EmbedController#best action checks if topic_id exists via TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url). If not found, it enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic and renders 'loading'. The TopicRetriever has throttling (retrieved_recently? checks redis with 60 second expiry) and perform_retrieve creates the TopicEmbed. However, if the retrieval fails (e.g., invalid URL, network error, no embed_by_username configured, or the external page can't be parsed), no TopicEmbed is created. The page will reload every 30 seconds, and after the 60-second throttle expires, it will try again. This creates an infinite loop of reloads and job enqueues for URLs that can never be successfully imported. The finding correctly identifies there's no terminal failure state - the loading page just keeps reloading forever.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — Every new embed URL invokes a full feed poll from its retrieval job, allowing many distinct page URLs to fan out into repeated feed fetches and imports.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lib/topic_retriever.rb:41, the code in perform_retrieve() does call Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) when feed_polling_enabled? is true. This means every time a new embed URL is retrieved, if RSS polling is enabled, it will execute the full feed poll job. However, this is intentional design - the code first checks if the embed already exists, and the feed poll is meant to potentially find the content via RSS before falling back to HTTP fetch. The 'retrieved_recently?' throttle at line 22-31 prevents the same URL from being processed more than once per 60 seconds. While multiple different URLs could trigger multiple feed polls, this is a design choice rather than a bug - the feed poll itself should be idempotent (it only imports content that doesn't already exist based on content_sha1). The finding describes expected behavior rather than a defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:36 — The importer advances content_sha1 without checking whether the post revision saved, causing a failed update to be marked complete and skipped on later polls.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 30-37, when updating an existing embed: `revisor.revise!(user, absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, bypass_rate_limiter: true)` is called, and then immediately `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` is executed. The `revise!` method in lib/post_revisor.rb returns the result of various operations but the return value is not checked. If the revision fails (e.g., `@post.save` returns false), the code still proceeds to update the content_sha1, marking the content as successfully updated when it wasn't. This means on subsequent polls, the content won't be re-attempted because the sha1 matches, even though the actual post content was never updated. This is a real bug - the content_sha1 update should be conditional on the revision succeeding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — The resize protocol sends the full referrer URL as targetOrigin, so embeds on normal path URLs reject the message and cannot resize.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment: the postMessage is using the full referrer URL as targetOrigin instead of just the origin (scheme+host+port), which causes the message to be rejected/dropped and prevents resizing from working. Both comments point to the same bug in the same file (embed.html.erb) with the same consequence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — A worker failure between SETNX and EXPIRE leaves a permanent throttle key so this embed URL will never be retrieved again.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 25-31, the pattern is: `if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the worker crashes or fails between SETNX succeeding and EXPIRE being called, the key will exist permanently without an expiration. This means the throttle check `retrieved_recently?` would always return true for that embed_url, preventing it from ever being retrieved. This is a real race condition/reliability bug - the SETNX and EXPIRE are not atomic, and a failure between them leaves orphaned keys.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15 — Concurrent imports can both observe no embed and the loser raises on the unique index instead of treating the other import as success.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in app/models/topic_embed.rb, the import method checks if an embed exists with `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if blank, creates a new one. However, there's a unique index on embed_url (seen in the migration). If two concurrent requests both see no embed and try to create one, the second will fail with a unique constraint violation. The code doesn't handle this race condition - it doesn't rescue the unique constraint error or use upsert/find_or_create_by with proper locking. This is a real concurrency bug that could cause errors in production when multiple requests try to import the same URL simultaneously.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:36 — The content hash is advanced even when the revisor fails to save the post, preventing a later poll from retrying that update.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 30-38, when updating an existing embed: the revisor.revise! is called, and then embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1) is called unconditionally on line 37. The revise! method returns a boolean indicating success/failure, but this return value is not checked. If revise! fails (returns false), the content_sha1 is still updated, which would prevent future retries from detecting that the content needs to be updated. This is a real bug - the hash update should be conditional on the revision succeeding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — force: true` drops any existing topic_embeds table before recreation, permanently losing embed mappings if this migration is rerun.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`. The `force: true` option in Rails migrations drops the table if it exists before creating it. However, this is a new migration file being added (the file path shows it's a new file with `new file mode`). In the context of Rails migrations, each migration is typically run only once and tracked in the schema_migrations table. While `force: true` could theoretically cause data loss if the migration were somehow run again on a database that already has the table with data, this is an edge case. The more concerning issue is that this is a new migration for a new feature, and the table shouldn't exist yet. The use of `force: true` in migrations is generally considered a code smell but in practice for a new migration introducing a new table, it's unlikely to cause real problems in normal operation. The finding overstates the risk - migrations aren't typically 'rerun' in production environments.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — force: true` drops any existing top_topics table before recreation, permanently losing its data when the migration is rerun.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points to `force: true` in the create_table statement for top_topics. Looking at the diff, this is a new migration file (20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) being added. The `force: true` option will drop the table if it exists before creating it. However, this is a migration file - migrations are typically run once and tracked. If the migration is run again (which shouldn't happen in normal operation), it would indeed drop data. But this is a new migration being added, and the table presumably doesn't exist yet. The real concern would be if someone runs migrations in a non-standard way or if the migration is re-run. While `force: true` is generally not recommended in migrations for production safety, this is more of a best practice/style concern rather than an immediate bug in the code being added. The migration will work correctly on first run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — Calling the scheduled job's execute method directly couples request retrieval to scheduler behavior, so either flow cannot evolve independently.

adjudication.rationale: The finding criticizes calling Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) directly in perform_retrieve. Looking at the code in lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 38-42, when a topic embed doesn't exist and feed polling is enabled, it directly instantiates and executes the PollFeed job synchronously. This is a design/architecture concern about coupling, not a bug or correctness issue. The code will function correctly - it will poll the feed and check if the embed exists. The finding is about code organization and future maintainability, which is a style/design preference rather than a concrete defect. The code works as intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:10 — This ActiveRecord model combines remote fetching, HTML normalization, and post creation/revision, making every import-stage change modify a persistence boundary shared by unrelated callers.

adjudication.rationale: The finding describes a design/architecture concern about the TopicEmbed model combining multiple responsibilities (remote fetching, HTML normalization, post creation/revision). While this is a valid observation about code organization, it is not a bug, security issue, or correctness problem. It's an architectural/design opinion about separation of concerns. The code as written will function correctly - it imports content, creates posts, and updates them as expected. This is a style/design nit rather than a real defect that would cause incorrect behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — Each hourly run materializes and imports every feed item with no entry bound or freshness cutoff.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the poll_feed.rb code at lines 27-35, the `poll_feed` method iterates over `rss.items.each` and calls `TopicEmbed.import` for each item. Looking at the `TopicEmbed.import` method in topic_embed.rb, it checks if an embed already exists for the URL (`embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`) and only creates a new topic if `embed.blank?`. If the embed exists, it only updates if the content hash changed. So while the code does iterate through all feed items, it doesn't actually 're-import' them - it skips items that already exist with the same content. The finding claims there's 'no entry bound or freshness cutoff' but the existing embed check effectively prevents duplicate imports. However, the concern about 'no entry bound' is partially valid - if a feed has thousands of items, it will iterate through all of them each hour, making database queries for each. This is an efficiency concern but not a correctness bug since duplicates are prevented.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:40 — Every cache-miss embed retrieval synchronously runs the full feed poll, so distinct embed URLs can repeatedly fetch and process the entire feed.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lib/topic_retriever.rb:40, the perform_retrieve method checks if feed_polling_enabled? and if so, calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}). This is called synchronously during the retrieve operation. Looking at app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the poll_feed method fetches the entire RSS feed and processes all items. The finding is correct - every time a cache miss occurs for an embed URL (when retrieved_recently? returns false), if feed polling is enabled, it will synchronously execute the full feed poll job. This means multiple distinct embed URLs could each trigger a full feed fetch and processing, which is inefficient. However, there is throttling via retrieved_recently? that prevents the same URL from being retrieved more than once per 60 seconds. The issue is that different embed URLs will each trigger the full feed poll. This is a real performance/efficiency concern in the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — Direct retrieval calls `open(url)` without requiring `open-uri`, so the retrieval job can fail as a local-file open and leave the embed loading indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at app/models/topic_embed.rb:48, the `import_remote` method calls `open(url).read`. However, at the top of the file (line 1), there's `require_dependency 'nokogiri'` but no `require 'open-uri'`. The `open` method without `open-uri` would try to open a local file, not a URL. However, looking at the broader context, in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 7, there's `require 'open-uri'` which would be loaded when that job runs. But `import_remote` in topic_embed.rb can be called independently (e.g., from lib/topic_retriever.rb:50 via `TopicEmbed.import_remote`). The topic_retriever.rb doesn't require 'open-uri' either. So when `import_remote` is called from `fetch_http` in topic_retriever.rb, `open-uri` may not be loaded, causing `open(url)` to fail or behave incorrectly. This is a real bug - the file relies on `open-uri` being loaded elsewhere but doesn't require it itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — A failure between `SETNX` and `EXPIRE` leaves the throttle key without a TTL, permanently suppressing later retrieval attempts for that URL.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 24-30, the pattern is: `if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes or fails between SETNX succeeding and EXPIRE being called, the key will exist without a TTL, meaning it will persist indefinitely. This would permanently block retrieval attempts for that specific embed_url. This is a real race condition/reliability bug - the atomic SET with EX option (or SETEX) should be used instead to avoid this window of failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:37 — The content SHA is recorded even if `PostRevisor#revise!` did not persist the update, so a failed feed update will not be retried.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 30-38, when updating an existing embed: `revisor.revise!(user, absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, bypass_rate_limiter: true)` is called, and then immediately `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` is executed. The `revise!` method in lib/post_revisor.rb returns a boolean indicating success, but this return value is not checked before updating the content_sha1. If the revision fails for any reason (e.g., database error, validation failure despite skip_validations), the content_sha1 will still be updated, causing future import attempts to think the content hasn't changed and skip the update. This is a real bug where failed updates won't be retried.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — One malformed feed item can raise during the loop and, with retries disabled, prevent all later entries from importing on every poll.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the code iterates over rss.items with `rss.items.each do |i|`. Inside the loop, it accesses `i.link`, `i.id`, `i.content`, and `i.title`. If any of these operations raise an exception (e.g., if `i.content` is nil and `.scrub` is called on it, or if CGI.unescapeHTML receives invalid input), the exception would propagate up and stop processing of all remaining items. With `sidekiq_options retry: false` set, the job won't retry, meaning all subsequent feed items would be skipped until the next hourly poll. This is a real robustness issue - one malformed item can prevent processing of all other valid items in the feed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — Untrusted RSS item HTML is persisted with raw_html cooking, allowing a compromised feed to store and execute script in the forum origin.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 33-34, RSS content is processed: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and then passed to `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)`. In app/models/topic_embed.rb, the import method creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (line 21). In app/models/post.rb lines 131-133, when cook_method is raw_html, the cook method returns `raw` directly without sanitization: `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. This means untrusted RSS content containing malicious JavaScript would be stored and rendered as-is, creating an XSS vulnerability. The RSS feed content is external/untrusted, and it's being rendered without HTML sanitization when displayed to users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — The initial hostname check is bypassed after an allowed embed URL redirects because open follows redirects to an arbitrary internal address.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in app/models/topic_embed.rb:48, the import_remote method uses `open(url).read` to fetch content from a URL. The method does check that the URL starts with 'http://' or 'https://' in the import method (line 11), but import_remote is called directly from topic_retriever.rb:50 via `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)`. The topic_retriever.rb does validate the host in `invalid_host?` method (line 14-18), checking that `SiteSetting.embeddable_host == URI(@embed_url).host`. However, the finding claims that if the allowed URL redirects to an internal address, the hostname check is bypassed. This is a valid concern because Ruby's `open-uri` follows HTTP redirects by default, and the hostname validation only checks the initial URL, not the final destination after redirects. An attacker could set up an allowed external URL that redirects to an internal service (SSRF attack). This is a real security vulnerability in the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:39 — The no-embed spec expects the removed TopicRetriever call instead of the new Jobs.enqueue contract, so it will fail and leaves enqueue arguments unverified.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the test in spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:39-44, it expects TopicRetriever.new to be called and then retriever.retrieve to be called. However, looking at the actual controller code in app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:14, when topic_id is nil, it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)` - not TopicRetriever directly. The test mocks TopicRetriever but the controller actually enqueues a job. This means the test expectations don't match the actual implementation, so the test would fail or pass incorrectly (the mocked expectations won't be met by the actual code path). This is a real test/implementation mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:5 — Feed-polling tests only mock poll_feed and never exercise parsing, link/id fallback, or TopicEmbed.import.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points out that the poll_feed_spec.rb tests only verify that poll_feed is called under certain conditions, but don't test the actual parsing logic, link/id fallback, or TopicEmbed.import integration. Looking at the diff, the test file at spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb only tests the execute method's conditional logic (checking if feed_polling_enabled?, feed_polling_url, and embed_by_username are set) and mocks poll_feed. The actual poll_feed method in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb contains significant logic including RSS parsing, URL extraction with fallback (url = i.id if url.blank?), and calling TopicEmbed.import - none of which is tested. However, this is a test coverage concern/suggestion rather than a bug or defect in the code itself. The code may work correctly; the tests are just incomplete. This is more of a code quality/testing best practice observation rather than a real defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:31 — Retriever specs mock private control flow and omit the Redis throttle/bypass and feed-or-HTTP retrieval paths.

adjudication.rationale: The finding criticizes the test coverage in topic_retriever_spec.rb, claiming it mocks private control flow and omits certain test paths. Looking at the spec file, it does mock `retrieved_recently?` and `perform_retrieve` which are private methods. However, this is a test design/coverage concern, not a bug or defect in the actual code. The tests are validating the public `retrieve` method's behavior under different conditions. While the tests could be more comprehensive, the finding is essentially a code review style suggestion about test quality rather than identifying an actual bug, security issue, or correctness problem in the implementation code itself.
